name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Iran says 4 tankers hit 11–12 Nov; strait shut
summary: Iran says four tankers hit mines in Hormuz 11–12 Nov and the strait stays shut until US meets its terms; blockade holds
state: Iran's military said four tankers were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz on 11–12 Nov, and UKMTO reported a ship hit by a projectile off Ras Al-Khaimah on 11 Nov (Baird Maritime, 12 Nov, citing Reuters). On 11 Nov Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the strait stays shut until the US meets seven conditions, including lifting its naval blockade (Al Jazeera). On 12 Nov President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran (Khaleej Times). Attacks on Gulf shipping set the Alert.
for_you: Anyone with travel or business in the Gulf should follow FCDO travel advice, which can change quickly. Disruption tends to push up fuel, shipping and insurance costs.
rubric_hit: Attacks on Gulf shipping: 4 tankers reported hit in Hormuz 11–12 Nov, strait closed by Iran (Alert)

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
